input.summary: Delete Vendor exclusivity obligation on Customer
input.comment: [Playbook] We cannot commit to a sole-supplier arrangement, and this clause also contradicts Section 12.3, so we have deleted it. If some protection is needed we could look at exclusivity for one defined product category for 12 months, ending automatically if service levels are missed.

[Playbook] We do not give suppliers most-favoured-nation rights in our other commercial arrangements, and this also conflicts with Section 12.3, so we have removed it. MFN pricing in our favour remains welcome.

input.summary: Delete USD 25,000/day liquidated damages payable by Customer
input.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us; delay in a Customer dependency is addressed through relief of Vendor's timeline, not a daily penalty. Service credits payable to us are of course fine.

input.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice window from 180 to 30 days

ops.oldText: one hundred eighty days' advance written notice
ops.newText: thirty days' advance written notice before the end of the then-current term

input.comment: [Playbook] A 180-day non-renewal window is well beyond our position; we have set it at 30 days (we can live with up to 60). The 12-month renewal term and the CPI/3% uplift cap in Section 8.3 are acceptable.

input.summary: Narrow non-solicit to involved personnel, 12 months, with carve-outs; delete no-hire

ops.oldText: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
ops.newText: For twelve months after the end of a person's involvement in the Services, neither Party will actively solicit for employment any personnel of the other Party who were directly involved in providing or receiving the Services. This does not restrict general advertisements or other recruitment efforts not targeted at such personnel, or the hiring of any person who responds to them or approaches a Party on an unsolicited basis.

input.comment: [Playbook] An 18-month restriction covering anyone employed by Vendor at any time, with no general-advertising carve-out and an "engage" no-hire element, is outside our position; we have narrowed it to a mutual 12-month non-solicit for personnel involved in the Services with the usual carve-outs.

input.summary: Limit audits to once a year on 30 days' notice; delete remote system access

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: Vendor may audit Customer's use of the Services no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, through an independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations. Vendor and its auditor have no right of access to Customer's systems, and Customer may satisfy an audit by providing usage records.

input.comment: [Playbook] Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems are walk-away territory; we have set the standard limits (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, no system access), consistent with the cost allocation already in Section 22.2.

input.summary: Add Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice

ops.text: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and no early-termination charge applies.

input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement runs for three years with no Customer right to exit without cause, so we have added a convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees.
